lede: Jon's Steelers at Patrick's Browns tonight: two teams at 2-1 who have both been outscored on the season, playing to the lowest total on the board. Then Sunday decides whether Mark keeps his lead.

beats.text: AFC North, 8:15 on Amazon. Pittsburgh has scored 23, then 3, then 30 — an offense nobody trusts behind a defense everybody does, coming off a strip-sack of Joe Burrow in the final minute. Cleveland has won two straight including the upset in Tampa, and has taken its last four home games against Pittsburgh. Jon is favored by a field goal and needs it more: he's two behind Mark, and Tennessee goes to Baltimore on Sunday as the week's heaviest underdog.

beats.tag: Mark · The one that could cost him
beats.text: Kansas City at Las Vegas on Sunday afternoon is the week's real pivot. Both teams are 3-0, Jon owns one and Mark owns the other, so a point moves from one of them straight to the other. Mark leads by two; this single game is the likeliest thing to make it one or three.

beats.tag: Patrick · A point he cannot lose
beats.text: Detroit at Carolina on Sunday night is his second civil war of the season — he owns both sidelines, so that point is banked before kickoff. Brian gets the same gift Monday night with Atlanta at New Orleans. Two of this week's sixteen games are settled already.

Two points in three weeks, and the market still likes him: the Rams are favored in Philadelphia against an Eagles team that may be without Jalen Hurts, and the Packers are favored in Tampa against a Buccaneers side starting Jalon Daniels with Baker Mayfield's thumb dislocated. If that doesn't produce something, nothing will.
